tests.notes: unsigned division discards the remainder; divide(7, 2) == 3
signed division truncates toward zero, not toward negative infinity; divide(-7, 2) == -3
signed modulo takes the sign of the dividend; mod(-7, 3) == -1, mod(7, -3) == 1
result type equals the base type; a signed base with an unsigned exponent is allowed
0 ** 0 == 1 and x ** 0 == 1, matching the EVM EXP opcode
uint8 + uint16 is computed in uint16, so add(255, 1) == 256 with no revert
compiles successfully; add(type(uint256).max, 1) reverts with Panic(0x11)
compiles successfully; sub(0, 1) reverts with Panic(0x11)
compiles successfully; mul(type(uint256).max, 2) and mulSigned(type(int256).min, -1) revert with Panic(0x11)
compiles successfully; pow(2, 256) reverts with Panic(0x11)
compiles successfully; divide(1, 0) reverts with Panic(0x12) because the divisor is not a compile-time constant
compiles successfully; mod(1, 0) reverts with Panic(0x12), the same code as division by zero
division of a literal by a literal zero is a compile-time error, unlike the runtime Panic(0x12) for non-constant divisors
no implicit common type between signed and unsigned integers, even at the same width
uint8 + uint16 has type uint16; assigning it to uint8 without an explicit cast is an implicit narrowing conversion
the exponent of ** must be unsigned, even when the base is unsigned
